title: Funeral Attendants
description: Perform a variety of tasks during funeral, such as placing casket in parlor or chapel prior to service, arranging floral offerings or lights around casket, directing or escorting mourners, closing casket, and issuing and storing funeral equipment.

tasks.text: Perform a variety of tasks during funerals to assist funeral directors and to ensure that services run smoothly and as planned.
Embalm, dress, cosmeticize, and casket the deceased.
Prepare obituaries for newspapers.
Transport the deceased to the funeral home.
Assist with cremations and the processing and packaging of cremated remains.
Close caskets at appropriate point in services.
Direct or escort mourners to parlors or chapels in which wakes or funerals are being held.
Place caskets in parlors or chapels prior to wakes or funerals.
Clean funeral parlors or chapels.
Arrange floral offerings or lights around caskets.
Clean and drive funeral vehicles, such as cars or hearses, in funeral processions.
Act as pallbearers.
Deliver floral arrangements or other items to family members of the deceased.
Carry flowers to hearses or limousines for transportation to places of interment.
Perform general maintenance tasks for funeral homes, such as maintaining equipment or caring for funeral grounds.
Obtain burial permits and register deaths.
Obtain doctors' signatures on death certificate and complete other paperwork, such as insurance claims forms.
Greet people at the funeral home.
Attend to the needs of the bereaved, such as by offering comfort, counseling, or after-care programs.
Offer assistance to mourners as they enter or exit limousines.
Perform various administrative tasks, such as typing documents or answering telephone calls.
Supervise funeral processions and assist with cemetery parking.
Issue and store funeral equipment.
Provide advice to mourners on how to make charitable donations in honor of the deceased.

skills.name: Social Perceptiveness
skills.def: Being aware of others' reactions and understanding why they react as they do.

skills.name: Service Orientation
skills.def: Actively looking for ways to help people.

skills.name: Active Listening
skills.def: Giving full attention to what other people are saying, taking time to understand the points being made, asking questions as appropriate, and not interrupting at inappropriate times.

skills.name: Speaking
skills.def: Talking to others to convey information effectively.

skills.name: Monitoring
skills.def: Monitoring/Assessing performance of yourself, other individuals, or organizations to make improvements or take corrective action.

skills.name: Coordination
skills.def: Adjusting actions in relation to others' actions.

skills.name: Reading Comprehension
skills.def: Understanding written sentences and paragraphs in work-related documents.

skills.name: Critical Thinking
skills.def: Using logic and reasoning to identify the strengths and weaknesses of alternative solutions, conclusions, or approaches to problems.

skills.name: Office suite software
skills.def: Software to provide word processing, spreadsheet, e-mail, presentations, or data management capabilities. Examples: Microsoft Office software.

skills.name: Spreadsheet software
skills.def: Software to create or edit numbers or text organized into rows and columns of cells. May include formulas which recalculate values based on other cells. Examples: Microsoft Excel.

skills.name: Word processing software
skills.def: Software to create, edit, store, or print documents. Examples: Microsoft Word.

skills.name: Accounting software
skills.def: Software to enable business functions relating to accounting, such as recording transactions or managing budgets. Examples: Bookkeeping software.

skills.name: Human resources software
skills.def: Software to manage employee evaluations, track wages or absenteeism, maintain safety records, or manage hours or time off. Examples: iCIMS Talent Cloud software.
